summary: Iteration 2 covers Binder view, Family trading (backend + UI) and Price history (collection + card). Backend: 11/11 new pytest tests pass against the public URL (members, compare, give, activity, collection_history, card_history + 404s); 20/20 regression tests still pass. UI: binder shows 18 pockets on desktop (2 pages/18 pockets) and 9 on mobile, page indicator correct ('Page 1–2 of 23'), binder-next-button, binder-prev-button and ←/→ arrow keys all flip pages, layout persists in localStorage key pb_set_layout across reload, grid toggle restores the grid+Owned/Missing chips. Owned Furret pocket renders full-colour (no grayscale class) once added. Family: created user A + user B via API, A added 3x swsh3-136 normal, B tracked swsh3 goal → A's /family page shows family-member-chips-<B id>, family-counts (1 only-you), i-can-give-grid contains give-card-swsh3-136 with 'Goal' badge + 2 spare; clicking give-card-swsh3-136-give and give-confirm-button succeeds, family-activity log receives the gift. Price history: collection-value-chart present on Dashboard and /collection (shows 'History started today' with 1 point as expected), card-price-chart renders on card detail (uses cardmarket trend when only 1 point).

design_issues.screen: Card detail / Dashboard / My Cards charts
issues: Recharts briefly logs 'width(-1) and height(-1)' warning during initial mount before container measures itself. Cosmetic console noise only; chart renders correctly immediately after. Could set an explicit minWidth={0} on <ResponsiveContainer> or wrap in a sized parent to silence.

critical_code_review_comments: family.py _give_list(): spare_qty calculation is a bit confusing — for single-variant cards it correctly reports (variant_qty - 1), but for multi-variant cards it reports (total_qty - 1) regardless of the chosen spare_variant. That can over-report spares when the chosen variant only has 1 copy but another variant has many. Consider: spare_qty = max(0, max_variant_qty - 1).
family.py give(): no transaction / rollback — if add_item to recipient fails after the sender's quantity was already decremented, the copy is lost. Low risk on local Mongo but worth a note.

history.collection_history forces a snapshot_user() on every GET; cheap, but means the 'first point' is created the moment the chart is first opened. Fine for UX ('History started today') but documents an implicit side-effect of a GET.
server.py still uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown (same note as iteration_1).

Binder.jsx: `pages[1]?.length` is used to decide whether to show the dash in 'Page X–Y of N'. If the last spread on desktop has <=9 cards, only one page is drawn — correct — but p1+1 is still the right-side index, so the fallback is correct. OK.

Charts.jsx CardPriceChart: when backend returns empty cardmarket_trend AND only 1 point, chart body may be empty; copy still says 'Cardmarket 30/7/1 day averages' which may be misleading. Low priority.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows (binder, family, charts). Scan upload UI step hit a hidden <input type=file> selector collision in the test harness and was skipped — scan backend already covered by regression + iteration_1 UI test.

test_credentials: admin@pokebinder.local / admin123 (works). Ephemeral TEST users created via /api/auth/register with password secret123.
seed_data_creation: Each test run registers fresh test_fam_a_* / test_fam_b_* users; adds 3x swsh3-136 to A and swsh3 base goal to B. Idempotent; no cleanup needed (collection_items unique index on user_id+card_id+variant).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Family compare uses ObjectId; invalid-id yields 404 (not 400). Family members list returns ALL other accounts on the server (household model) — earlier iteration test users will be present. Price history: /collection/history calls snapshot_user() on every GET so the user ALWAYS gets at least 1 point (today) — chart UI gracefully handles 1-point case with 'History started today'. CardPriceChart falls back to cardmarket_trend when daily history has <2 points. localStorage key for binder layout is pb_set_layout. Full regression + new tests live under /app/backend/tests/ and run in ~9s total with pytest-xdist.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. The only test-script hiccup was a Playwright selector collision between the hidden camera input (data-testid=take-photo-input) and the Upload input on /scan; use data-testid='upload-photo-input' or the second input index to avoid the ambiguity.
